summary: Validated signature-pad fixes and new guided sequential signing flow on web preview via mouse drag. SIGNATURE PAD: pad opens on tap, empty-tap/single-click produces no path and does not enable Apply (Apply shows opacity 0.45 which is the disabled visual), helper text correctly says 'Draw your signature above — a tap alone won't count.', drag draws stroke, helper flips to 'Looks good. Add more strokes if needed, or tap Apply.', a second drag adds a 2nd persistent path (SVG shows 2 <path> elements, first does NOT vanish), Clear resets to 0 paths and re-disables apply, Apply commits and the field box turns solid green with the actual drawn SVG strokes rendered inside. GUIDED FLOW on sr_sc_01 (3 pages, 5 required fields): s_ack is the active current field, declaration disabled (opacity 0.45) and text reads 'Complete all required fields to confirm and sign.', tapping s_sign1 (out of order) does NOT open the editor and shows the lock-hint bar 'Please complete the highlighted field first.'. 'Next required field' button scrolls+opens s_ack, after acknowledgement the flow auto-advances to initials → s_sign1 → s_sign2; after the 5th field completes the declaration becomes tappable with the real declaration text and sign-submit opacity goes to 1. Submit routes to /status → processing → completed. REGRESSION on sr_loa_01: happy path (draw+apply signature → declaration → Sign and submit → status/processing/completed) passes end-to-end. First-open DEV badge reaches 'recorded (1 first-open event)' as expected. All 10 requested scenarios PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: review.tsx is ~478 lines — close to the 700 limit but fine; FieldOverlay/FieldEditor/SignatureThumb could be split into their own files for maintainability if the file grows further.

SignaturePad.tsx uses `hasInk`/`includes(' L ')` string checks on raw path strings — fine for mock, but if path format ever changes this heuristic could silently break; consider a counter of committed strokes instead.

Pressable `disabled` prop in react-native-web does not forward the HTML `disabled` attribute to a <button>, so Playwright's `is_disabled()` always returned false; the visual-disable (opacity 0.45) and the internal guard (apply early-returns when strokes.length===0 and onFieldPress short-circuits pending fields) still enforce the behaviour correctly, but automated accessibility tooling (axe) may misreport it. Consider adding `accessibilityState={{disabled: true}}` on `sig-apply` and `sign-submit` when gated.
seed_data_creation: None. All data comes from the in-memory mock adapter.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mock resets on full reload. Draw signatures with mouse press-down → move (steps=5+) → up (a single click produces no 'L' segment and is intentionally ignored). Prefilled fields on sr_loa_01: f_name/f_title/f_email → first active field is f_sign. On sr_sc_01 the first active field is s_ack on page 1; order after ack is s_initials → s_sign1 → s_sign2 (s_name prefilled, s_date read-only). Key testIDs: signature-pad, sig-apply, sig-clear, sig-cancel, field-<id>, next-field, lock-hint, declaration, sign-submit, ack-confirm, dev-firstopen. Pressable disabled state is visual (opacity 0.45) — don't rely on Playwright is_disabled(); instead assert opacity or that onPress is a no-op.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs reproduced this iteration. The previously-reported signature-pad empty/multi-stroke issues and the new guided-flow sequential lock all behave per spec.
